governance_note: Review additivity, proportionality, superposition, and coefficient stability.
State whether the linear model is local, global, exploratory, predictive, explanatory, or diagnostic.
Inspect residuals for curvature, thresholds, changing variance, subgroup differences, and time dependence.
Check whether variables modify each other's effects rather than contributing independently.
Review saturation, capacity limits, discontinuities, and regime changes.
Assess whether outputs influence future inputs or whether the transition matrix changes with state.
Determine whether averages hide subgroup, spatial, temporal, or network heterogeneity.
Flag predictions and scenarios outside observed or validated ranges.
Separate prediction, association, mechanism, and causal identification.
Explain what the linear model clarifies, what it omits, and where distortion risk is highest.
